gen-dafont-bloody-sora: Sora reads as a plain sans with geometric curves that stay widely parted and never swell at the corners. Bloody counters with big round bowls and a tall, commanding lowercase, while Sora keeps its own letters moderate and precise.
gen-dafont-bloody-space-grotesk: Bloody comes in tall and commanding, with big round bowls and no hairlines at all. Space Grotesk follows in a ribbon of constant width, its counters breathing open, so paragraphs of sans-serif text move along smoothly.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-fs-amulya: Amulya reads as a plain sans, contemporary and modern, with generous gaps left in every curve. And Bushcraft, with its widely spaced, unshaded letters and barely distinct capitals, supplies the expressive voice above it.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-fs-spline-sans: Bushcraft spaces its letters extra wide, and its capitals hardly stand above the lowercase, giving the heading an artistic, unhurried look. Spline Sans is the friendly counterweight.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-fs-synonym: Synonym reads as a plain sans, dependable and clean, laid down as a stripe of constant ink with generous openings. And a longer passage would move steadily, with Bushcraft's tall, wide-spaced letters left to carry the personality above.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-bree-serif: Bree Serif reads as a classic serif with literary polish, its outsized lowercase giving each line real presence on the page. Longer text would feel warm.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-outfit: Wide-spaced and artistic, with capitals that barely rise above the lowercase. Outfit, a plain sans with curves that stop short of closing, is the pair's strongest quality: a lean, cable-like line under a tall, expressive heading.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-plus-jakarta-sans: Bushcraft stretches its letters wide and tall, artistic and mostly closed in its shapes. Plus Jakarta Sans sits beside it as a modern, monoline sans-serif, its curve endings held open and precise.
gen-dafont-capture-it-bitter: Urban, towering and nearly sealed shut. Bitter, a slab-serif with a large lowercase and an open s, would carry a longer passage in a grounded, dependable way, easing off the heading's pressure.
gen-dafont-capture-it-fs-amulya: Amulya is a plain sans that keeps its curves generously open, a modern counterpart to the heading. Amulya's open, moderate letters set against Capture It's towering, nearly sealed forms make the pair's strongest quality.
